events.summary:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

San Antonio River at Hwy 72 near Runge affecting Goliad and
Karnes Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...San Antonio River at Hwy 72 near Runge.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 28.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 2:15 AM CDT Saturday was 28.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 33.7
feet tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage
early Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 27.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
32.9 feet on 05/28/2013.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Cibolo Creek Near Falls City affecting Karnes County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Cibolo Creek near Falls City.

* WHEN...Until tomorrow morning.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Major lowland flooding of crop and
pasturelands cut off many livestock and potentially drown them.
Widespread flooding reaches secondary and primary roads, low
bridges and crossings. Most of the Goliad State Park facilities
downstream are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 23.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 2:15 AM CDT Saturday was 23.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
this evening and continue falling to 1.9 feet early Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
23.1 feet on 06/17/1981.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Houston County in southeastern Minnesota...
Southwestern La Crosse County in west central Wisconsin...

* WHEN...Until 445 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Water over roadways. Overflowing poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 248 AM CDT, ongoing heavy rain has been falling and will
continue.Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms.
This  will cause urban and small stream flooding. Between 0.5 and
1.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
La Crosse, La Crescent, Onalaska, Holmen, French Island, La
Crosse Airport, Brice Prairie, Medary, Lock And Dam 7, Highway 33
And Losey Boulevard, Midway, and New Amsterdam.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
